criterion.name:
Interpretation of Sources
- Interpret each source to identify a perspective(s) -Explaining the linkage between principals of (globalization, nationalism, or liberalism)
Note: You must address ALL three sources.

description.text:
Interpretation of the source is sophisticated, insightful,
and precise, demonstrating a perceptive understanding of the principals: globalization, nationalism or liberalism.

Interpretation of the source is logical, specific, and
adept, demonstrating a sound understanding of the principals: globalization, nationalism or liberalism.

Interpretation of the source is adequate, straightforward,
and conventional, demonstrating a generalized
understanding of the principals: globalization, nationalism or liberalism.

Interpretation of the source is incomplete, vague, and
simplistic, demonstrating a confused understanding of the principals: globalization, nationalism or liberalism.

Interpretation of the source is scant, inaccurate,
irrelevant, and/or the source is copied, demonstrating
little or no understanding of the principals: globalization, nationalism or liberalism.

criterion.name:
Identification of Relationships
-identify/explain the relationships that exist among ALL sources -Support the relationships with evidence drawn from the sources and knowledge of Social Studies

description.text:
The explanation of relationship(s) is perceptive and
thorough.

The explanation of relationship(s) is capable and
purposeful.

The explanation of relationship(s) is adequate and
straightforward.

The explanation of relationship(s) is superficial,
incomplete, redundant, and of questionable accuracy

The explanation of relationship(s) is scant, illogical,
and tangential.

criterion.name:
Quality of Communication
-This includes the control of - Vocabulary, Sentence Structure, and Mechanics and Grammar
Note: You are expected to use paragraph form

description.text:
Vocabulary is precise and deliberately chosen. Sentence
structure is controlled and sophisticated. The writing
demonstrates skillful control of mechanics and grammar
and is judiciously organized.

Vocabulary is appropriate and specific. Sentence structure
is controlled and effective. The writing demonstrates
capable control of mechanics and grammar and is
purposefully organized.

Vocabulary is conventional and generalized. Sentence
structure is controlled and straightforward. The writing
demonstrates basic control of mechanics and grammar
and is adequately organized.

Vocabulary is imprecise, simplistic, and inappropriate.
Sentence structure is awkward. The writing demonstrates a
faltering control of mechanics and grammar and is
ineffectively organized.

Vocabulary is overgeneralized and inaccurate. Sentence
structure is uncontrolled. The writing demonstrates a
profound lack of control of mechanics and grammar and is
haphazardly organized.
Writers ability to Interpret, identify and communicate the sources is inaccurate,  illogical and irrelevant .
Writers ability to Interpret, identify and communicate the sources is simplistic,  superficial and vague.
Writers ability to Interpret, identify and communicate the sources is  straightforward,  adequate and conventional.
Writers ability to Interpret, identify and communicate the sources is effective,  capable and adept.
Writers ability to Interpret, identify and communicate the sources is  sophisticated,  perceptive and insightful.

criterion.name:
Analysis of Source
-Critically analyze the source -demonstrate an understanding of the source and its relationship to a perspective on globalization, nationalism or liberalism

description.text:
The analysis of the source is insightful and sophisticated;
a comprehensive understanding of the ideological
perspective(s) is demonstrated.

The analysis of the source is capable and adept;
a sound understanding of the ideological perspective(s)
is demonstrated.

The analysis of the source is conventional and
straightforward; a generalized understanding of the
ideological perspective(s) is demonstrated.

The analysis of the source is incomplete and lacks depth;
a confused understanding of the ideological perspective(s)
is demonstrated.

The analysis of the source is illogical, tangential, and/or the
source is simply copied; a minimal understanding of the
ideological perspective(s) is demonstrated.

criterion.name:
Argumentation
-Establishes a position -Develops arguments based on logic and reasoning -Establishes a relationship between position taken, argumentation and the sources perspective

description.text:
The position established is convincingly supported by
judiciously chosen and developed argument(s). The
argumentation is consistent and compelling, demonstrating
an insightful understanding of the assignment. The
relationship between the position taken, argumentation,
and the ideological perspective presented in the source is
perceptively developed

The position established is persuasively supported by
purposefully chosen and developed argument(s). The
argumentation is logical and capably developed,
demonstrating a sound understanding of the assignment.
The relationship between the position taken,
argumentation, and the ideological perspective presented
in the source is clearly developed.

The position established is generally supported by
appropriately chosen and developed argument(s). The
argumentation is straightforward and conventional,
demonstrating an adequate understanding of the
assignment. The relationship between the position taken,
argumentation, and the ideological perspective presented
in the source is generally developed.

The position established is confusing and largely unrelated
to the argument(s). The argumentation is repetitive,
contradictory, simplistic, and based on uninformed belief.
The relationship between the position taken,
argumentation, and the ideological perspective presented
in the source is superficially developed.

The position established has little or no relationship to the
source or arguments. The argumentation is irrelevant and
illogical. The relationship between the position taken,
argumentation, and the ideological perspective presented
in the source is minimally developed.

criterion.name:
Evidence
-Is relevant and accurate -Reflects depth and/or breadth of social studies knowledge -Evidence may be theoretical, historical, contemporary and/or current events

description.text:
Evidence is sophisticated and deliberately chosen. The
relative absence of error is impressive. A thorough and
comprehensive discussion of evidence reveals an insightful
understanding of social studies knowledge and its
application to the assignment.

Evidence is specific and purposeful. Evidence may contain
some minor errors. A capable and adept discussion of
evidence reveals a solid understanding of social studies
knowledge and its application to the assignment.

Evidence is conventional and straightforward. The evidence
may contain minor errors and a mixture of relevant and
extraneous information. A generalized and basic discussion
reveals an acceptable understanding of social studies
knowledge and its application to the assignment.

Evidence is potentially relevant but is unfocused and
incompletely developed. The evidence contains
inaccuracies and extraneous detail. The discussion reveals
a superficial and confused understanding of social studies
knowledge and its application to the assignment.

Evidence is irrelevant and inaccurate. The evidence
contains major and revealing errors. A minimal or scant
discussion reveals a lack of understanding of social studies
knowledge and its application to the assignment.

criterion.name:
Communication
- Fluency or essay organization -Syntax, mechanics and grammar -Use of vocabulary and social studies terminology

description.text:
The writing is fluent, skillfully structured, and judiciously
organized. Control of syntax, mechanics, and grammar is
sophisticated. Vocabulary is precise and deliberately
chosen. The relative absence of error is impressive.

The writing is clear and purposefully organized. Control of
syntax, mechanics, and grammar is capable. Vocabulary is
appropriate and specific. Minor errors in language do not
impede communication.

The writing is straightforward and functionally organized.
Control of syntax, mechanics, and grammar is adequate.
Vocabulary is conventional and generalized. There may be
occasional lapses in control and minor errors; however, the
communication remains generally clear.

The writing is awkward and lacks organization. Control of
syntax, mechanics, and grammar is inconsistent.
Vocabulary is imprecise, simplistic, and inappropriate.
Errors obscure the clarity of communication.

The writing is unclear and disorganized. Control of syntax,
mechanics, and grammar is lacking. Vocabulary is
overgeneralized and inaccurate. Jarring errors impede
communication.
Students position paper is unclear, illogical and inaccurate.
Students position paper is simplistic, unfocused and inconsistent.
Students position paper is straightforward, generalized and adequate.
Students position paper is adept, logical and capable.
Students position paper is insightful, compelling and sophisticated.
